lines.text: What if every person on Earth vanished, right now?
Eight billion people, gone in a blink. Cars roll to a stop. The city falls silent.
Two days later. With nobody running the power stations, the lights go out.
And without pumps, the subway tunnels fill with water.
One year. Weeds push up through cracks in the road, and wild animals wander the empty streets.
Twenty years. Streets buckle and cave in, cars rust away, and young trees grow right through the tarmac.

segments.caption: Steel gives way
segments.fact: BRIDGES FAIL WITHIN A FEW HUNDRED YEARS

lines.text: Three hundred years. Rust has eaten through the steel.
Bridges fall, and the towers begin to come down.
Five hundred years. Where the avenue used to be, there is a forest.
Vines cover the last walls, and deer graze where traffic once roared.
One hundred thousand years. Even the carbon we added to the air has faded.
A few stones and some buried plastic are all that say we were ever here.
So, what would you want to leave behind?
